texts.facts: The appeal and the cross-objection have been preferred challenging the judgment and award passed by Prl.Civil Judge and Addl M.A.C.T., Saundatti, at Saundatti (hereinafter referred as 'tribunal' for short) in MVC No.1057/2010 dated 06.06.2012. 2. The appeal preferred by the Insurance Company is premised on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded by the tribunal and seeking for reduction of the same. Whereas, the cross-objection preferred by the claimants is premised on the ground of inadequacy and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal. Consequently, seeking for enhancement of compensation. 3. Brief Facts of the case, 3.1 The unfortunate incident of road traffic accident in the present case has rendered the claimant Siddayya S/o Gangappa @ Maharudrayya Betsurmath incapable and immobile for the rest of his life forcing him to be bedridden for the remaining part of his life. On 21.08.2009, when the claimant who was working as a conductor in the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-22/B-9399 while on his duty from Hubli-Ilakal in the route assigned left the Ilakal at about 8:00 p.m and reached Badami at about 11:20 p.m. Some of the passengers alighted at Badami and when the bus reached the railway station road at about 11:30 p.m., on Badami-Guledagudda road, the driver of the vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and safety and dashed to a road side Neelagiri tree and caused the accident. Due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus in which the claimant was the conductor, sustained severe grievous injuries all over his body. Immediately thereafter, the claimant was admitted to Community Health Centre, Badami where he took first aid treatment. Later, he was shifted to Kerudi Hospital, Bagalakote, wherein he was inpatient from 22.08.2009 to 24.08.2009. Subsequently, the claimant was admitted to Vivekanand General Hospital, Deshpande Nagar, Hubli wherein he was inpatient from 24.08.2009 to 12.09.2009 and underwent operation. Again the claimant was admitted to Navadagi Hospital, Saundatti on 12.9.2009 and thereafter, he was admitted to Kulgod Multi Specialty Hospital, Ramdurg from 11.10.2009 to 12.11.2010. 3.2 It is stated that the claimant underwent several surgeries and operations and expended huge financial amount towards the medical treatment and follow up treatment. It is further stated that prior to the occurrence of accident, claimant was working as a conductor in the offending bus and was earning Rs.8,000/- per month and maintaining his family. He was unmarried and aged about 22 years. Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, claimant is permanently disabled and he is bedridden for life. The movements of both the legs are restricted, he cannot stand, walk or sit and The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/ 3 requires two attendants on a daily basis for his day to day activities. As earlier stated, claimant is a bachelor thereby he has lost the marriage prospects and due to the enormous injuries suffered in the accident, he is mentally depressed and has suffered enormously both physically and financially. In view of having sustained serious permanent disability forcing the claimant to be bedridden for the remaining part of his life and having incurred huge financial expenditures, the claimant filed claim petition, seeking compensation. 3.3 On notice being served to respondents, who appeared before the Court and filed their statement of objections inter-alia denying the occurrence of accident, rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending bus. The respondents also denied the age, avocation and income of the claimant, apart from denying exorbitant amount of compensation sought for by the claimant. It is also pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license, as on the date of occurrence of accident and further the driver of the bus had violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy. On the basis of these pleadings, sought for dismissal of the claim petition. 4. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal has framed relevant issues for consideration. 5. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined three other witnesses including one Doctor-Dr.Sanjeev Kalasur as PW.4 and got marked documents as Exs.P.1 to P.538. Whereas, the respondents have not adduced any evidence. However, they got marked the insurance policy as Ex.R.1 with the consent of parties.
texts.arguments: 7. Being aggrieved by the exorbitant, unreasonable compensation awarded, the insurance company has preferred appeal challenging the judgment and award of the tribunal. Being aggrieved by the inadequacy and meager compensation awarded, the claimant has preferred cross-objection seeking enhancement of compensation. It is vehement contention of learned counsel Shri G.N.Raichur, appearing on behalf of the appellant-Insurer that the tribunal has committed a serious error in awarding huge and exorbitant compensation contrary to the material evidence placed on record both oral and documentary. He further contends that the tribunal has grossly erred in considering the disability to an extent of 100% believing the evidence of PW.4-Dr. Sanjeev Kalasur. Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has gone on a tangent by awarding excess compensation under various heads without keeping in mind the award of compensation towards disability at 100%. He contends that the tribunal has erred in awarding compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of loss of amenities. When already the tribunal has arrived at compensation towards loss of income due to disability at 100%, the question of awarding further compensation under the head of loss of amenities would not arise and that runs contrary to the principles of awarding loss of income due to the disability. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/ 4 8. Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has also erred in awarding other compensation under the head pain and suffering, attendant charges, conveyance, incidental charges, future medical expenses, which are highly exorbitant and the same requires to be set-aside, as it is against the intent of legislation in awarding the compensation under the guise of just and reasonable compensation. 9. Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has committed a gross error in awarding future medical expenses and thereby the total compensation being highly exorbitant and unreasonable, the same requires to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned counsel further contends that while awarding compensation tribunal and this Court will have to consider reasonable and just compensation to be awarded rather than the compensation being a luxury to the claimant and becoming a huge loss to the insurance company. On these grounds learned counsel for the appellant seeks to allow this appeal, consequently [LEAKAGE_MASK] the judgment and award of the tribunal and reduce the compensation by awarding just and reasonable compensation. 10. Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimant who has preferred cross objection has sought for enhancement of compensation in view of - 10 - the compensation being meager and inadequate. It is his vehement contention that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is arbitrary, unreasonable and wholly erroneous and contrary to the material evidence placed on record. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the claimant that he suffered permanent physical disability and has thereby lost the capacity to work or earn in future and that due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending bus, the young and energetic adolescent man, claimant herein has been rendered immobile and incapable for the rest of his life to be forced to be bedridden and to be dependent on other persons for remaining part of his life. 11. It is vehement contention of the learned counsel that though tribunal has accepted the disability to an extent of 100%, the tribunal has committed a gross error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation under several heads. It is his primary contention that the tribunal has failed to take into account the proper income for assessment of loss of future income and has committed an error in taking the income at only - 11 - Rs.4,500/- per month, whereas, the claimant has adduced evidence by stating that he was a conductor by profession while he was on his duty as a conductor, traveling from Hubballi to Ilkal and back, he suffered the injuries rendering him bedridden for the remaining part of his life due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus. It is the contention of the claimant that though he was earning Rs.8,000/- per month, the tribunal has failed to take into consideration the said amount for assessment of compensation, thereby the tribunal has committed a serious error in calculation of compensation towards loss of income towards permanent disability. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/ 5 12. It is further contended by the learned counsel for the claimant that due to the claimant being rendered bedridden and disabled for the remaining part of his life, the future marriage prospects of the claimant has been totally diminished and there is absolutely no scope for any marriage prospect for the claimant, which aspect has been ignored and not considered and no amount of compensation is awarded under this head. Learned - 12 - counsel also contends that the tribunal has failed to take into consideration awarding of future prospects while granting compensation, which is another serious error committed by the tribunal. He also contends that the claimant admittedly was inpatient in the hospital for more than a year and the tribunal has not awarded reasonable compensation towards loss of income during the laid up period. He further contends that the tribunal has lost sight of the fact the claimant is now rendered helpless and dependent on another person to do is day to day activities which aspect has also been ignored and no amount of compensation is awarded by the tribunal for attendant to attend to the future life of the claimant, which requires 24 x 7 treatment by the attendant. On these aspects the learned counsel seeks to allow his cross objection and consequently enhance the compensation substantially as claimed in the claim petition. 13. Having heard the learned counsel for the insurer Shri G.N.Raichur and the learned counsel for the - 13 - claimant Shri H.M.Dharigond, the points that arise for consideration before this Court are as under: i) Whether the tribunal has committed error in awarding exorbitant compensation to the claimant? ii) Whether the tribunal has awarded inadequate and meager compensation to the claimant? iii) Whether the tribunal has not considered the relevant aspects for determination of compensation to be in the form of just and reasonable compensation? iv) What order? 14. It is not in dispute that on 21.8.2009 when the claimant was travelling in the bus, as mentioned above as a conductor doing his official duty, the driver of the said bus drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and dashed against a Nilgiri Tree and caused the accident. It The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/ 6 is not in dispute that due to the accident the claimant suffered injuries. - 14 - 15 . In order to substantiate that the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the bus, and that he was responsible for rash and negligent driving, the claimant has produced Exs.P.1 to P.5, which are all police records. In view of this Court assessing income of the claimant at Rs.5,000/- per month, the future prospects at 40% will have to be added in consonance to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680. 20. The learned counsel for the claimant says, at least Rs.4,000/- would be required for engaging at least one attendant to take care of the claimant at 24 x 7 basis for day to day activities of the claimant. The learned counsel for the insurer vehemently contends relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, for the purpose of not awarding any amount of compensation under the head pain and suffering and loss of amenities on the ground that when 100% disability is taken, question of awarding further compensation under these two heads does not arise. However, I am afraid that the contention put forth by the learned counsel for the insurer cannot be accepted for the reason that no amount of monetary compensation can heal the mental scar of pain and agony suffered and undertaken or met by the claimant presently or in future - 20 - on the basis of day to day activities. These monetary amounts could be only a solace to the claimant to meet his expenses and it cannot bring back the original life of claimant with similar enthusiasm and energy in life. The learned counsel for the insurer vehemently contends that the said amount awarded by the tribunal itself is exorbitant and the same does not require further enhancement and he continues to rely on the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra). 27. The learned counsel for the insurer submits that the Court cannot grant compensation more than what is claimed by the claimant.
